greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. Grace and peace be with you as we gather in the light of God’s word.

Lord, have mercy.
Christ, have mercy.

psalm_response: Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
homily:
We often walk through our days like travelers in a crowded marketplace, jostled by the noise, the demands, and the sheer speed of life. In today’s Gospel, we see a scene that feels startlingly familiar: a crowd so dense, so frantic, that people are actually trampling one another. It is a portrait of anxiety—a world where everyone is trying to get ahead, where everyone is afraid of being left behind, where the pressure to perform and to be seen can crush the very spirit that makes us human. Into that chaos, Jesus speaks a word that is meant to stop us in our tracks. He tells us, 'Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins? Yet not one of them has escaped the notice of God.'

Think of a sparrow. It is a small, common, easily overlooked creature. It doesn't have the majesty of an eagle or the song of a nightingale. It is just a bird, flitting from branch to branch, often unnoticed by the hurried passerby. Yet Jesus uses this image to anchor our entire existence. He isn’t just talking about birds; he is talking about the secret, quiet, overlooked details of your life—the things you think no one sees, the moments of ache you carry in the silence of your heart, the prayers you whisper when you are alone in the dark. He is saying that God is not a distant observer, but one who counts the very hairs on your head. He is saying that you are held in an attention so precise, so intimate, that nothing—not one tear, not one memory, not one heartbeat—is ever lost.

Benjamin Vo lived with a heart that seemed to understand this mystery of being seen. He was a boy who looked at the world with a brilliant, searching curiosity, yet his focus was never on the 'crowd' or the 'trampling.' Whether he was diving into the complexities of cloud infrastructure, coding games with a sophistication that surprised the adults around him, or simply sitting in the quiet of a room with his family, Ben was a boy who knew the value of the small, the hidden, and the gentle. He didn't need the spotlight. He found his joy in the 'con chim airlines'—a vision of flight that he shared with his father, a dream that was as much about the connection they shared as it was about the jets themselves. He was a boy who could look at his own piggy bank and, without a moment of hesitation, offer it all to help his uncle. He didn't need to break it, or empty it, or tell the world of his kindness. The offer, made in the quiet of his own heart, was the truth of who he was. It was a sign that he lived not for the applause of the crowd, but for the love of the Father.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these four months, the silence of your home has been a heavy companion. You remember the way Ben would come to you with his ideas, his plans, his gentle smile. You remember the way he would listen—truly listen—to the stories his dad would tell, finding joy in the simple, quiet connection of a father and son. That bond is not a thing of the past. It is a living, breathing reality. It is the truth that St. Paul speaks of in the first reading: 'In him you also, who have heard the word of truth... were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.' That seal is a mark of belonging that death cannot touch. You are a family of four, and that is a truth that is anchored in the promise of the One who is the Resurrection and the Life. You are not being asked to carry the weight of the past; you are being asked to walk into the future with the promise of the Resurrection as your light.

I want to speak very gently to the ache that visits you in the quiet of the night. There is a weight that parents often carry, a stone of wondering if they missed something, if they could have done more, if they could have changed the outcome. I want to lift that stone from you today. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his sanctuary. You were the ones who nurtured that brilliant, curious, gentle spirit. You did not miss anything. God does not look at your son’s life and find it lacking, and He does not look at your care for him and find it wanting. You are not being accused. You are being held. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of self-reproach. That is a weight that has no place in the kingdom of God. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the secret language of that love. You know that Ben is not gone; he has simply gone ahead to the place where all the 'con chim airlines' finally take flight. You are the one who carries the legacy of his curiosity, his kindness, and his smile. When you sit down to code, or when you look up at the clouds, know that you are not doing it alone. You are a family of four, and that bond is stronger than death. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the brother who knows that the most important things in life are not the things we possess, but the love we share. You are a witness to the fact that love is the only thing that actually lasts.

Look at the Gospel again. Jesus says, 'Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but after that can do no more.' This is the hinge of our hope. It is the realization that the power of death is limited, but the power of God’s love is infinite. We spend so much of our lives afraid of the things that can hurt us—afraid of the loss, afraid of the silence, afraid of the future. But Jesus invites us to fear only the One who can hold our souls in His hands. And that One is not a judge waiting to catch us out; He is the Father who counts the hairs on our heads. He is the one who saw Ben’s smile, who heard his laughter, and who holds every single one of his dreams in the palm of His hand.

Think of the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a perfect image of what you are doing. You are taking the love that was poured into Ben, and you are letting it flow into the lives of others. You are ensuring that his life is not a closed chapter, but a living, breathing, life-sustaining force. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are turning the soil of the earth so that the Kingdom can grow. You are the ones who are keeping his light burning in a world that so often forgets to look up.

There is a profound freedom in realizing that we do not have to hold it all together. We do not have to be the ones who provide the answers. We are children of the promise. We are heirs to a kingdom that is not built by human hands, but by the grace of God. That grace is the 'bread' we need for the journey. It is the strength that comes when our own strength is gone. It is the peace that settles over us when we finally stop fighting the silence and start listening to the voice of the Father.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you in His tender care. Go in peace, knowing you are held by the One who counts every sparrow.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ.
For all who grieve, that the Lord console them, heal their hearts, and fill them with the hope of the Resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
In Christ we were also chosen,
destined in accord with the purpose of the One
who accomplishes all things according to the intention of his will,
so that we might exist for the praise of his glory,
we who first hoped in Christ.
In him you also, who have heard the word of truth,
the Gospel of your salvation, and have believed in him,
were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,
which is the first installment of our inheritance
toward redemption as God’s possession, to the praise of his glory.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R.  (12) Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
Exult, you just, in the LORD;
praise from the upright is fitting.
Give thanks to the LORD on the harp;
with the ten-stringed lyre chant his praises.
R. Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
For upright is the word of the LORD,
and all his works are trustworthy.
He loves justice and right;
of the kindness of the LORD the earth is full.
R. Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
Blessed the nation whose God is the LORD,
the people he has chosen for his own inheritance.
From heaven the LORD looks down;
he sees all mankind.
R. Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
At that time:
So many people were crowding together 
that they were trampling one another underfoot.
Jesus began to speak, first to his disciples,
“Beware of the leaven–that is, the hypocrisy–of the Pharisees.“There is nothing concealed that will not be revealed,
nor secret that will not be known.
Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness
will be heard in the light,
and what you have whispered behind closed doors
will be proclaimed on the housetops.
I tell you, my friends,
do not be afraid of those who kill the body
but after that can do no more.
I shall show you whom to fear.
Be afraid of the one who after killing
has the power to cast into Gehenna;
yes, I tell you, be afraid of that one.
Are not five sparrows sold for two small coins?
Yet not one of them has escaped the notice of God.
Even the hairs of your head have all been counted.
Do not be afraid.
You are worth more than many sparrows.”

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben
